title: Calculation or Decision Only Available Through the Mutation That Applies It
pattern: Non-trivial domain calculation or decision logic (allocations, pricing, eligibility, classification) is implemented inside the method that mutates entity state or performs database/external I/O, with no side-effect-free function that computes the same result.
why_bad: The rule can only be exercised by performing the change: previews, dry-runs, reports and "what if" calculations mutate the entity or hit the database, and unit tests of the business rule need a real or mocked store. Mixing the decision with I/O also hides which part failed when the write succeeds but the decision is wrong, and vice versa.
detection: A method taking `&mut self` or a database/client handle whose body computes a result or decision from inputs and state (arithmetic over collections, threshold comparisons, enum classification) and in the same body writes fields or performs I/O, where no pure function or `&self` method exposes that computation.
counterexample: Operations whose check and update must be atomic (compare-and-swap, token-bucket consume, seat reservation under a lock), which must stay combined though they may additionally offer a pure preview; trivial commands whose "calculation" is the assignment itself; orchestration handlers that call a pure domain function and then persist its result.
source: Eric Evans, *Domain-Driven Design* (2003), Ch. 10 "Side-Effect-Free Functions"; Scott Wlaschin, *Domain Modeling Made Functional* (2017), Ch. 10; Vaughn Vernon, *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (2013), Ch. 10.
